key: A batsman in a gully cricket match is
name: ch01_gully_batsman_excuses
alt: A gully cricket batsman walks off with his stumps knocked flat behind him, muttering excuses while the other players point at the broken wicket.
scene: A wide street-level view of a narrow residential lane in an Indian town, late afternoon, washing lines and a parked scooter in the background. On the LEFT, a cricket wicket made of three sticks stands in front of a painted brick wall; the middle and off stumps are flying backwards through the air with small motion lines, and a red rubber ball rolls away. Above the wicket, a large bold label reads "OUT". In the CENTRE, a teenage batsman (about 16, white T-shirt, rolled-up jeans, rubber slippers) walks away towards the right holding his bat low, chin up, eyebrows knotted, mouth mid-mutter. A big thought bubble rises from his head showing three tiny grievances: a foot over a chalk crease, a bumpy pitch, and a scowling umpire. Inside the bubble a bold label reads "ROBBED". On the RIGHT, the bowler (a thin boy in a striped shirt) and two fielders, one a younger girl in a school pinafore, stand together pointing back at the broken stumps with open mouths, plainly seeing what happened. Behind them the boy acting as umpire, a slightly older cousin in a cap, stands with one finger raised. Warm golden light, cheerful but wry mood: everyone sees the stumps fly except the batsman.

key: In a joint family, ask each person who
name: ch01_joint_family_kitchen_mess
alt: Three family members stand around a messy kitchen, each pointing away from themselves with a NOT ME speech bubble.
scene: A front-on view of a small Indian joint-family kitchen in the morning: a granite counter with a two-burner gas stove, a steel pressure cooker, a stack of unwashed steel plates, a pan with leftover instant noodles, spilled turmeric and onion peels across the counter, and a steel dabba lid on the floor. The mess fills the centre of the picture. Three family members stand in front of the counter, spaced left to right. LEFT: a teenage boy (about 15, oversized hoodie, earphones round his neck) holding a fork, shrugging with palms up. CENTRE: an uncle in his fifties in a pressed office shirt and trousers with a laptop bag on his shoulder, glancing at his wristwatch, already half turned towards the door. RIGHT: a grandmother in a cotton sari with reading glasses, arms folded, chin raised, pointing her thumb towards the others. Each has a white speech bubble above their head, and each bubble contains the same bold label "NOT ME"; thin arrows from each person point sideways at someone else, forming a little circle of blame around the mess. Soft morning light through a small window with a steel grille, gently comic mood: each one sincerely believes their own story and the kitchen stays dirty.

key: Touch the leaves of a chhui-mui
name: ch01_touch_me_not_plant
alt: Split picture: a poking finger makes a touch-me-not plant fold shut, while sunlight and water let the same plant open wide.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, the same small touch-me-not plant with feathery double-row leaves growing beside a dusty village path in both halves. LEFT panel: a large adult hand comes in from the top left, index finger poking a leaf; the leaves nearest the finger and along the whole stem are snapped shut, folded flat against the stalks, the plant drooping and closed up like a clenched fist. Small motion lines show the quick folding, and a dashed arrow bounces off the closed leaves to show that nothing gets in. A bold label above reads "CRITICISM". RIGHT panel: the same plant now wide open, every leaflet spread flat and green, a small round pink flower puff on top. A warm sun shines from the upper right with soft rays, and a simple tin watering can held by a child's hand (a girl of about eight in a yellow frock, only her arm and shoulder visible) pours a gentle stream of water at the roots. A bold label above reads "CARE". Ground in both panels is reddish village soil with a few pebbles and a low mud wall behind. Calm, clear morning light; the mood moves from tense on the left to relaxed and growing on the right.

key: A mother in Hyderabad shouts at her
name: ch01_helmet_mother_asks
alt: Split picture: a shouting mother gets a helmet hung on the scooter mirror; when she asks why and buys a lighter helmet, her son wears it.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, both halves set at the gate of an apartment building in an Indian city in the morning, a scooter parked in front. LEFT panel: the mother (late 40s, salwar kameez, dupatta, hand on hip) leans out of the gate shouting, other arm pointing, three jagged lines coming from her mouth. Her son (about 19, college backpack, T-shirt and jeans) rides off down the lane with the heavy black full-face helmet hanging from the rear-view mirror, not on his head, his hair blowing; a small red cross badge floats beside the dangling helmet. A bold label above reads "SHOUTING". RIGHT panel: the same mother stands calmly beside the son at the gate, head tilted, one hand open in a questioning gesture; a small speech bubble shows a heavy helmet with a little headache zigzag next to a lighter open-face helmet with a tick. The son sits on the scooter wearing a light sky-blue open-face helmet, strap buckled, smiling and giving a thumbs up. A green tick badge floats beside his head. A bold label above reads "ASKING WHY". Bright morning light, a neem tree beside the gate, mood moving from frustrated to cooperative.

key: Two partners built a popular chai-and
name: ch01_chai_partners_split
alt: Two former partners run rival chai stalls facing each other while customers split between them and a third chain down the road draws the big crowd.
scene: A wide street view of a busy Indian city road in the evening, read left to right. LEFT: a small chai-and-snacks stall with a striped awning in teal, a large steel kettle and glass jars of biscuits; the senior partner (late 50s, grey moustache, white kurta) stands in front of it, scowling and pointing angrily across the road with one arm. Opposite him, in the CENTRE-LEFT, a near-identical stall with an amber awning; the junior partner (early 30s, checked shirt, apron) stands behind the counter with arms spread, puzzled and defensive. Between the two stalls a jagged crack runs across the pavement, and a bold label "SPLIT" sits above the crack. A thin line of five customers holding small paper chai cups divides in two, half walking to each stall, looking unsure. On the far RIGHT, further down the road, a larger third stall with a plum awning and bright bulbs is crowded with a big queue of customers, several carrying takeaway cups, all facing away from the feuding pair; a bold label above it reads "THIRD CHAIN". Dashed arrows show customers drifting from the two small stalls towards the third. Warm streetlight glow, a sense of a quarrel nobody wins.

key: A housing society secretary is caught
name: ch01_society_secretary_defends
alt: At a housing society meeting, residents shout and wave papers at the secretary, who stands with arms crossed behind a shield of excuses.
scene: An interior view of the common hall of an Indian housing society in the evening: plastic chairs, a tube light, a notice board with a paint-colour chart pinned on it, and a folding table at the front with a steel water jug. On the LEFT and centre, four residents half-rise from their chairs, shouting: a woman in a nightgown-style kaftan waving a printed quote sheet, an elderly man with a walking stick, a young man in a gym vest pointing, and a middle-aged woman in a sari with her hand cupped to her mouth. Jagged shout lines fly from them towards the right. On the RIGHT, behind the table, the society secretary (early 60s, half-sleeve shirt, spectacles, pen in pocket) stands with arms tightly crossed, chin up, eyes half closed, unmoved; in front of him floats a large curved pale shield, and the shout lines bounce off it with little sparks. Above him a speech bubble holds the bold label "NOT MY FAULT". A small paint bucket and a roller sit on the floor beside the table to show what the fight is about, with a price tag showing "2x". A bold label at the top centre reads "SOCIETY MEETING". Harsh tube-light glow, tense but slightly comic mood: shouting is loud, and it changes nothing.

key: A college student in Kochi posts an
name: ch01_meme_hostel_confrontation
alt: A mocking meme spreads across phones, then the angry classmate turns up at the poster's hostel door while friends hold them apart.
scene: A two-part illustration read left to right, set in a college in coastal Kerala. LEFT third: a large smartphone floats in the air showing a chat group screen with a crude cartoon meme of a stick figure with big ears; around it, three smaller phones held by laughing hands show the same image, connected by dashed arrows spreading outwards, to show the screenshot copying itself. A bold label above the phones reads "MEME". RIGHT two-thirds: a hostel corridor with green-painted walls, a coconut palm visible through a window, and a wooden door standing open with a room number "14" on it. In the doorway, the student who made the meme (about 19, vest and shorts, phone in hand) leans back in shock, palms up. Facing him, the mocked classmate (about 19, college ID card on a lanyard, glasses) jabs a finger forward, furious, with jagged anger lines above his head. Two friends stand between them, one in a mundu and T-shirt pushing the angry classmate back with both hands, another in a football jersey holding the meme-maker by the shoulder. A bold label at the top right reads "PAYBACK". Late evening yellow corridor light, tense, a moment before a fight is stopped.

key: A team captain in a club cricket final
name: ch01_captain_deletes_message
alt: In the dressing room after a lost final, the captain deletes a long angry draft to his bowler, remembering his own tired, shaking hands.
scene: An interior of a small cricket club dressing room in the evening: wooden benches, kit bags, pads and a helmet on hooks, a ceiling fan, a small window showing floodlights. On the RIGHT, the young opening bowler (about 22, sweaty white cricket kit, towel on his head) sits slumped on a bench, elbows on knees, staring at the floor. On the LEFT, the captain (late 20s, white kit with a cap, sunburnt face) stands holding his phone; an oversized phone screen floats beside him showing many grey lines of a long draft message with angry red marks, and a bold label "DRAFT" across its top. His thumb is pressing a trash-bin icon, and a curved arrow shows the draft sliding into the bin, with a bold label "DELETE" beside the bin. A thought bubble above the captain shows two small memories: a blazing sun over a field with a scoreboard reading "18 OV", and his own hands trembling while holding a ball. In the middle, faint, a rolled practice net and a few balls suggest the nets session to come. Warm tired light, mood of anger cooling into patience; the bowler has not yet seen the phone.

key: A pressure cooker in an Indian kitchen
name: ch01_pressure_cooker_whistle
alt: A pressure cooker lets off steam through its whistle while a writer drops a furious letter into a drawer marked unsent instead of the post.
scene: A cosy Indian kitchen-and-study corner seen front-on. LEFT half: a large steel pressure cooker on a blue gas flame, its whistle lifted and a tall cheerful plume of white steam rising and curling upward, the lid sitting firmly in place. Little dashed lines show pressure inside escaping only through the whistle. A bold label beside the steam reads "LET OFF STEAM". RIGHT half: a wooden desk by a window. A middle-aged man (late 40s, vest and lungi, reading glasses pushed up on his forehead) has just finished writing an angry letter: the paper is covered in jagged scribble lines with a large exclamation mark, a pen lies beside it, and a little steam puff rises from his head mirroring the cooker. Next to him his wife (mid 40s, cotton sari, calm half-smile) gently lifts the folded letter out of a wire tray labelled with a small envelope icon and slips it into an open desk drawer. On the drawer front a bold label reads "UNSENT". A red post box is visible through the window, empty and untouched. A dashed arrow runs from the cooker's steam to the man's head-steam to link the two. Warm evening kitchen light, relieved, calm mood.

key: At a family wedding, a young cousin
name: ch01_wedding_uncle_remark
alt: Split picture: at a wedding an uncle makes a dismissive remark about a cousin's job offer, and twenty years later the grown cousin still remembers it.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: a bright Indian wedding reception, marigold garlands and fairy lights strung overhead, round tables in the background. A young cousin (about 22, new kurta, beaming) holds up his phone showing a simple offer letter with a tick. Facing him, a senior uncle (early 60s, safari suit, big moustache, glass of juice in hand) leans in with a smirk; a large spiky speech bubble comes from his mouth containing a small office building with a dismissive hand wave. The cousin's smile is cracking, and a small jagged crack badge appears over his chest. A bold label at the top reads "WEDDING". RIGHT panel: a quiet, grey, rainy courtyard at a funeral twenty years later, a framed photo with a garland on a small table. The same cousin, now in his early 40s with greying temples and a white kurta, stands with hands folded, looking down. A soft thought bubble above him shows the wedding moment again in miniature: the smirking uncle and the spiky speech bubble, still sharp and vivid. A bold label at the top reads "20 YEARS LATER". Left side warm and festive, right side muted and still; the one sentence lasts.

key: Two senior doctors in a busy government
name: ch01_two_doctors_hospital
alt: Split picture of a hospital ward: one doctor snaps at a ward boy in front of patients, the other calmly asks a nurse what happened and fixes it.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, both halves showing the same crowded government hospital ward with iron beds, green curtains, a ceiling fan and an IV stand. LEFT panel: a senior doctor (mid 50s, white coat, stethoscope, spectacles) stands with one arm thrust out, mouth wide, jagged shout lines flying at a young ward boy (about 20, khaki uniform) who shrinks back, holding a dropped steel tray; two patients in beds and a visiting relative watch with wide, uneasy eyes. A small red exclamation badge floats over the ward boy. A bold label at the top reads "SNAPS". RIGHT panel: a second senior doctor (early 50s, woman, white coat over a sari, stethoscope) stands beside a junior nurse (mid 20s, white uniform and cap) near an IV stand, leaning in with an open hand, calm, listening; the nurse points at a tangled IV line and the doctor's hand is straightening it. A green tick badge floats over the IV stand, and the patients in the beds look relaxed, one smiling. A bold label at the top reads "FIXES". Even, bright daylight from tall windows; the mood moves from tense and humiliating on the left to calm and capable on the right.

key: A new cook at a busy dhaba in Punjab
name: ch01_dhaba_kheer_mistake
alt: In a dhaba kitchen, a crying young cook stands by mixed-up salt and sugar jars while the owner rests a kind hand on his shoulder.
scene: An interior of a busy roadside dhaba kitchen in Punjab: a big clay tandoor in the back, steel shelves with large unlabelled-looking jars, a huge aluminium pot of kheer on a low flame, and steam in the air. In the CENTRE foreground, two big identical glass jars sit on the counter, one tipped open with white crystals spilling; above them small bold labels on the jars read "SALT" and "SUGAR", and a curved dashed arrow shows a ladle went into the wrong jar. Beside the pot, the new cook (about 19, white vest, apron, a small cloth cap) stands with head bowed and a tear on his cheek, hands clasped. On the RIGHT, the dhaba owner (mid 50s, Sikh man with a turban and grey beard, kurta-pyjama, a big steel bracelet) rests a large reassuring hand on the cook's shoulder and smiles; a speech bubble from him shows a small calendar page reading "SUN" and a bowl of kheer with a tick, meaning tomorrow you make it again. In the background through a serving hatch, a cheerful wedding party crowd is visible. A bold label at the top centre reads "SECOND CHANCE". Warm golden kitchen light, mood of embarrassment turning into trust.

key: A mother in a Mumbai flat during board
name: ch01_board_exam_corrections
alt: A mother surrounded by a pile of correction bubbles stops when her stressed daughter quietly brings her a cup of chai.
scene: An interior of a small Mumbai flat living room at night, a study table under a lamp heaped with textbooks, a printed mock test sheet showing "78" in red, and a window with city lights. LEFT: the mother (mid 40s, house kurta, hair in a bun, dupatta over the shoulder) stands with one finger raised, and from her mouth rises a tall tottering stack of many small speech bubbles, each containing a tiny symbol: a straight-back stick figure, a phone with a cross, the number 78, a plate with a cross; the stack nearly touches the ceiling. Beside the stack a bold label reads "CORRECTIONS" with a long row of tally marks under it. RIGHT: the daughter (15, school T-shirt and pyjamas, tired eyes, pencil behind her ear) walks towards her mother holding out a small steaming glass of chai with both hands, a shy smile. A small grey cloud hangs over the daughter's head, showing she carries her own stress. The mother's face is caught mid-realisation, eyebrows lifting, the last speech bubble half-faded. A bold label above the chai reads "ONE KIND ACT". Warm lamp light against dark blue night, quiet and tender mood.

name: ch01_auto_driver_reasons
alt: An auto driver refuses a short trip; a thought bubble reveals the traffic jam he would sit in and the rising fuel price behind his refusal.
scene: A street view at a busy Bengaluru auto stand at nine in the morning, rain trees overhead and a metro pillar in the background. On the LEFT, a young office-goer (late 20s, formal shirt, ID lanyard, laptop bag) stands with arms spread in irritation, a small grey storm cloud with a zigzag over his head. In the CENTRE, a yellow-and-green three-wheeler auto-rickshaw is parked at the kerb, and the driver (mid 40s, khaki uniform shirt, moustache, towel on the shoulder) leans out from the driver seat shaking his head with a weary, not unkind face. Between the two men a bold label reads "WHY?". Above the driver rises a large thought bubble that opens up his reasons: on the left side of the bubble, a long gridlock of cars and buses with a small auto stuck in the middle and a clock face showing forty minutes passing; a bold label "JAM" sits over the gridlock; on the right side of the bubble, a fuel pump nozzle with an upward red arrow. A faint dashed line links the passenger's eyes to the thought bubble to show he now sees it too, and his storm cloud is fading at the edges. Bright, hazy morning light, mood shifting from anger to understanding.
